verses.1:1: The words of Amos, which came in Accarim in Tekoa, which he saw concerning Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah king of Judah and in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joash king of Israel, two years before the earthquake.
verses.1:2: And he said, "The Lord has sounded forth from Zion, and from Jerusalem He has given His voice; and the pastures of the shepherds mourned, and the summit of Carmel dried up."
verses.1:3: And the Lord said, "For three impieties of Damascus, and for four, I will not turn away from him, because they sawed with iron saws the women with child among those in Gilead.
verses.1:4: And I will send forth fire into the house of Hazael, and it shall devour the foundations of the son of Hader.
verses.1:5: And I will shatter the bars of Damascus, and I will utterly destroy the inhabitants from the plain of On, and I will cut down a tribe from the men of Haran; and the called people of Syria shall be taken captive," says the Lord.
verses.1:6: Thus says the Lord: "For three impieties of Gaza, and for four, I will not turn away from them, because they took captive the captivity of Solomon, to shut them up in Idumea.
verses.1:7: And I will send forth fire upon the walls of Gaza, and it shall devour its foundations.
verses.1:8: And I will utterly destroy the inhabitants from Ashdod, and a tribe shall be removed from Ashkelon; and I will bring My hand upon Ekron, and the remnant of the foreigners shall perish," says the Lord.
verses.1:9: Thus says the Lord: "For three impieties of Tyre, and for four, I will not turn away from her, because they shut up the captivity of Solomon in Idumea, and did not remember the covenant of brethren.
verses.1:10: And I will send forth fire upon the walls of Tyre, and it shall devour her foundations."
verses.1:11: Thus says the Lord: "For three impieties of Idumea, and for four, I will not turn away from them, because they pursued his brother with a sword, and he ravaged a mother upon the earth, and he seized his shuddering for a testimony, and he kept his onslaught for victory.
verses.1:12: And I will send forth fire into Teman, and it shall devour the foundations of its walls."
verses.1:13: Thus says the Lord: "For three impieties of the sons of Ammon, and for four, I will not turn away from him, because they ripped open the women with child of the Gileadites, that they might enlarge their own borders.
verses.1:14: And I will kindle fire upon the walls of Rabbah, and it shall devour its foundations with a cry in the day of war, and it shall be shaken in the days of its consummation;
verses.1:15: and its kings shall go into captivity, their priests and their rulers together," says the Lord.
verses.2:1: Thus says the Lord: "For three impieties of Moab, and for four, I will not turn away from him, because they burned the bones of the king of Idumea into lime.
verses.2:2: And I will send forth fire upon Moab, and it shall devour the foundations of its cities; and Moab shall die in weakness, with a shout and with the sound of a trumpet.
verses.2:3: And I will utterly destroy a judge from its midst, and all who belong to it I will slay with him," says the Lord.
verses.2:4: Thus says the Lord: "For three impieties of the sons of Judah, and for four, I will not turn away from him, because they cast away the law of the Lord and did not keep His ordinances; and their vanities which they made led them astray, after which their fathers followed.
verses.2:5: And I will send forth fire upon Judah, and it shall devour the foundations of Jerusalem."
verses.2:6: Thus says the Lord: "For three impieties of Israel, and for four, I will not turn away from him, because they sold a righteous man for silver, and a needy man for the sake of sandals,
verses.2:7: that tread upon the dust of the earth; and they struck the heads of the poor with fists, and turned aside the way of the humble; and a son and his father went in to the same maidservant, that they might profane the name of their God.
verses.2:8: And binding their garments with cords, they made curtains beside the altar, and they drank wine from extortion in the house of their God.
verses.2:9: Yet I removed the Amorite from before their face, whose height was like the height of a cedar, and he was strong as an oak; and I dried up his fruit from above and his roots from beneath.
verses.2:10: And I brought you up from the land of Egypt, and led you about in the wilderness forty years, to inherit the land of the Amorites.
verses.2:11: And I took from your sons for prophets, and from your young men for sanctification. Are these things not so, O sons of Israel?" says the Lord.
verses.2:12: "And you gave the sanctified ones wine to drink, and you commanded the prophets, saying, 'You shall by no means prophesy.'
verses.2:13: Therefore, behold, I am rolling beneath you, in the manner that a wagon full of straw rolls.
verses.2:14: And flight shall perish from the runner, and the mighty man shall by no means hold fast his strength, and the warrior shall by no means save his life;
verses.2:15: and the archer shall by no means stand his ground, and the one swift with his feet shall by no means escape safely, nor shall the horseman save his life;
verses.2:16: and the mighty man shall not find his heart in mighty deeds; the naked man shall flee in that day," says the Lord.
verses.3:1: Hear this word which the Lord has spoken against you, O house of Israel, and against every tribe which I brought up out of the land of Egypt, saying:
verses.3:2: "You only have I known from all the tribes of the earth; therefore I will avenge all your sins upon you."
verses.3:3: Will two walk together at all, unless they make themselves known to one another?
verses.3:4: Will a lion roar out of his forest when he has no prey? Will a young lion give his voice out of his den at all, unless he has seized something?
verses.3:5: Will a bird fall upon the earth without a fowler? Will a snare be sprung upon the earth without catching anything?
verses.3:6: Will a trumpet sound in a city, and a people not be terrified? Will there be calamity in a city which the Lord has not done?
verses.3:7: For the Lord God will by no means do anything unless He reveals instruction to His servants the prophets.
verses.3:8: A lion will roar, and who will not fear? The Lord God has spoken, and who will not prophesy?
verses.3:9: Proclaim to the regions among the Assyrians and upon the regions of Egypt, and say, "Assemble yourselves upon the mountain of Samaria, and behold many wondrous things in its midst, and the oppression that is in it."
verses.3:10: "And she did not know what things shall be before her," says the Lord, "those who store up unrighteousness and misery in their regions."
verses.3:11: Therefore thus says the Lord God: "O Tyre, your land round about shall be made desolate, and he shall bring down your strength from you, and your regions shall be plundered."
verses.3:12: Thus says the Lord: "Just as when the shepherd snatches out of the mouth of the lion two legs or the lobe of an ear, so shall the sons of Israel who dwell in Samaria be snatched out opposite the tribe, and in Damascus the priests."
verses.3:13: "Hear and testify against the house of Jacob," says the Lord God Almighty,
verses.3:14: "for in the day when I avenge the impieties of Israel upon him, I will also take vengeance upon the altars of Bethel, and the horns of the altar shall be demolished and shall fall to the ground.
verses.3:15: I will confound and strike the colonnaded house upon the summer house; and ivory houses shall perish, and many other houses shall be added," says the Lord.
verses.4:1: Hear this word, you heifers of Bashan who are on the mountain of Samaria, who oppress the poor and trample the needy, who say to their masters, "Bring to us, that we may drink!"
verses.4:2: The Lord swears by His holy things: "Behold, days are coming upon you, and they shall take you away with weapons, and fiery pestilent men shall cast those who are with you into cauldrons heated from beneath,
verses.4:3: and you shall be carried out naked, one opposite another, and you shall be cast away to Mount Romman," says the Lord.
verses.4:4: "You entered into Bethel and acted ungodly, and at Gilgal you multiplied ungodliness; and you brought your sacrifices in the morning, and your tithes every three days.
verses.4:5: And they read the law outside, and proclaimed confessions. Declare that the sons of Israel have loved these things," says the Lord God.
verses.4:6: "And I will give you aching of teeth in all your cities, and lack of bread in all your places; yet you did not return to Me," says the Lord.
verses.4:7: "I also withheld the rain from you three months before the vintage; and I will send rain upon one city, and upon another city I will not send rain; one portion shall be rained upon, and the portion upon which I will not send rain shall wither.
verses.4:8: And two and three cities shall gather together to one city to drink water, and they shall by no means be satisfied; yet you did not return to Me," says the Lord.
verses.4:9: "I struck you with scorching heat and with blight; you multiplied your gardens; the caterpillar devoured your vineyards, your fig groves, and your olive groves; yet not even thus did you return to Me," says the Lord.
verses.4:10: "I sent forth death upon you in the way of Egypt, and I slew your young men with the sword, together with the captivity of your horses; and I brought up your camps in fire in your wrath; yet not even thus did you return to Me," says the Lord.
verses.4:11: "I overthrew you as God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah, and you became like a firebrand snatched out of the fire; yet not even thus did you return to Me," says the Lord.
verses.4:12: "Therefore thus I will do to you, O Israel; and because I will do thus to you, prepare yourself to call upon your God, O Israel."
verses.4:13: For He who establishes thunder and creates spirit, and declares His Anointed to men, who makes dawn and mist, treading upon the high places of the earth—the Lord God Almighty is His name.
verses.5:1: Hear this word of the Lord which I take up against you as a lamentation: "The house of Israel
verses.5:2: has fallen; it shall never rise again. The virgin of Israel has stumbled upon his land; there is no one to raise her up."
verses.5:3: Therefore thus says the Lord, the Lord: "As for the city from which a thousand went out, a hundred shall be left; and from which a hundred went out, ten shall be left to the house of Israel."
verses.5:4: For thus says the Lord to the house of Israel: "Seek Me, and you shall live;
verses.5:5: but do not seek Bethel, and do not enter into Gilgal, and do not cross over to the Well of the Oath; for Gilgal shall surely be led into captivity, and Bethel shall be as though it did not exist."
verses.5:6: Seek the Lord and live, lest the house of Joseph blaze up like fire and devour it, and there be no one to quench it for the house of Israel.
verses.5:7: He who executes judgment on high, and has set righteousness upon the earth;
verses.5:8: He who makes all things and transforms them, and turns shadow into morning, and darkens day into night; who calls for the water of the sea and pours it out upon the face of the earth—the Lord is His name;
verses.5:9: He who apportions ruin against strength, and brings distress upon the fortress.
verses.5:10: They hated him who reproves in the gates, and they abhorred a holy word.
verses.5:11: Therefore, because they struck the poor with their fists and you accepted choice gifts from them, you have built houses of hewn stone, yet you shall by no means dwell in them; you have planted desirable vineyards, yet you shall by no means drink the wine from them.
verses.5:12: For I know your many ungodly deeds, and your sins are mighty, trampling down the righteous, taking bribes, and turning aside the needy in the gates.
verses.5:13: Therefore he who has understanding shall keep silent at that time, for it is a time of wicked men.
verses.5:14: Seek good and not evil, that you may live; and so the Lord God Almighty shall be with you, just as you have said:
verses.5:15: "We have hated evil things and loved good things." And restore judgment in the gates, so that the Lord God Almighty may have mercy on the remnant of Joseph.
verses.5:16: Therefore thus says the Lord God Almighty: "In all the streets there shall be wailing, and in all the highways they shall say, 'Woe! Woe!' The farmer shall be called to mourning and wailing, and to those who know lamentation;
verses.5:17: and in all the roads there shall be wailing, for I will pass through the midst of you," said the Lord.
verses.5:18: Woe to those who desire the day of the Lord! To what end is this day of the Lord to you? Indeed, it is darkness and not light,
verses.5:19: just as if a man flees from the face of a lion, and a bear falls upon him, and he leaps into his house and leans his hands against the wall, and a serpent bites him.
verses.5:20: Is not the day of the Lord darkness, and not light? And is it not gloom, having no brightness?
verses.5:21: "I have hated, I have rejected your feast days, and I will by no means smell sacrifices in your festive assemblies.
verses.5:22: For though you offer to Me your burnt offerings and sacrifices, I will not accept them; neither will I look upon your peace offerings of display.
verses.5:23: Remove from Me the sound of your songs, and I will not listen to the melody of your instruments.
verses.5:24: And judgment shall roll down like water, and righteousness like an impassable torrent.
verses.5:25: Did you offer Me slain beasts and sacrifices in the wilderness for forty years, O house of Israel?
verses.5:26: Yes, you took up the tabernacle of Moloch and the star of your god Rephan, their images which you made for yourselves;
verses.5:27: and I will carry you away into exile beyond Damascus," says the Lord; God Almighty is His name.
verses.6:1: Woe to those who despise Zion, and to those who trust in the mountain of Samaria! They have harvested the firstfruits of the nations, and they themselves have entered in. O house of Israel,
verses.6:2: cross over, all of you, and see; and pass on from there to Hamath Rabbah, and go down from there to Gath of the foreigners, the mightiest of all these kingdoms—see whether their borders are greater than your borders.
verses.6:3: Those who come to an evil day, who draw near and lay hold of false sabbaths;
verses.6:4: those who sleep upon beds of ivory and live luxuriously upon their couches, and eat kids from the flocks and sucking calves from the midst of the herds;
verses.6:5: those who clap to the sound of musical instruments—they reckoned these things as abiding and not as fleeting;
verses.6:6: those who drink strained wine and anoint themselves with the finest ointments, and suffered nothing over the ruin of Joseph.
verses.6:7: Therefore now they shall be captives from the forefront of the rulers, and the neighing of horses shall be removed from Ephraim.
verses.6:8: For the Lord has sworn by Himself: "I abhor all the arrogance of Jacob, and I have hated his lands; and I will remove the city with all who dwell in it."
verses.6:9: And it shall come to pass, if ten are left in one house, that they shall die, and the survivors shall be left behind;
verses.6:10: and their own relatives shall take them up and strive earnestly to carry their bones out of the house; and one shall say to those who are over the house, "Is there still anyone with you?" And he shall say, "No more." And he shall say, "Keep silent, so as not to mention the name of the Lord."
verses.6:11: For behold, the Lord commands, and He shall strike the great house into fragments and the small house into clefts.
verses.6:12: Shall horses pursue among rocks? Shall they keep silent among mares? For you have turned judgment into wrath, and the fruit of righteousness into bitterness—
verses.6:13: you who rejoice over nothing at all, who say, "Have we not obtained horns by our own strength?"
verses.6:14: "For behold, I am raising up a nation against you, O house of Israel," says the Lord of hosts, "and they shall afflict you so that you do not enter into Hamath, and as far as the torrent of the west."
verses.7:1: Thus the Lord God showed me: and behold, a brood of locusts coming at dawn, and behold, one creeping locust—Gog the king.
verses.7:2: And it shall be, if he finishes devouring the grass of the land—and I said, "O Lord, Lord, be merciful! Who shall raise up Jacob? For he is very small.
verses.7:3: Relent, O Lord, concerning this." "And this shall not be," says the Lord.
verses.7:4: Thus the Lord showed me: and behold, the Lord summoned judgment by fire, and it devoured the great deep, and devoured the portion of the Lord.
verses.7:5: And I said, "O Lord, cease now! Who shall raise up Jacob? For he is very small.
verses.7:6: Relent, O Lord, concerning this." "And this shall by no means come to pass," says the Lord.
verses.7:7: Thus the Lord showed me: and behold, He was standing upon a wall of adamant, and in His hand was adamant.
verses.7:8: And the Lord said to me, "What do you see, Amos?" And I said, "Adamant." And the Lord said to me, "Behold, I am setting adamant in the midst of My people Israel; I will no longer continue to pass by him.
verses.7:9: And the altars of laughter shall be destroyed, and the sacred rites of Israel shall be made desolate, and I will rise up against the house of Jeroboam with a sword."
verses.7:10: Then Amaziah the priest of Bethel sent to Jeroboam king of Israel, saying, "Amos is forming conspiracies against you in the midst of the house of Israel; the land is by no means able to bear all his words.
verses.7:11: For thus says Amos: 'Jeroboam shall die by the sword, and Israel shall be led away captive from his land.'"
verses.7:12: And Amaziah said to Amos, "O seer, go, depart into the land of Judah, and live out your life there, and there you shall prophesy;
verses.7:13: but at Bethel you shall no longer continue to prophesy, for it is a sanctuary of the king, and it is a house of the kingdom."
verses.7:14: Then Amos answered and said to Amaziah, "I was not a prophet, nor was I the son of a prophet; rather, I was a goatherd and one who pierces sycamore figs.
verses.7:15: And the Lord took me from the sheep, and the Lord said to me, 'Go, prophesy against My people Israel.'
verses.7:16: And now hear the word of the Lord: You say, 'Do not prophesy against Israel, and you shall by no means stir up a crowd against the house of Jacob.'
verses.7:17: Therefore thus says the Lord: 'Your wife shall play the harlot in the city, and your sons and your daughters shall fall by the sword, and your land shall be measured out by a line, and you yourself shall die in an unclean land, and Israel shall be led away captive from his land.'" Thus the Lord, the Lord showed me:
verses.8:2: And behold, a fowler's basket. And He said, "What do you see, Amos?" And I said, "A fowler's basket." And the Lord said to me, "The end has come upon My people Israel; I will no longer continue to pass by him.
verses.8:3: And the paneled ceilings of the temple shall wail in that day," says the Lord, the Lord. "Many are the fallen in every place; I will cast silence."
verses.8:4: Hear these things now, you who crush the needy in the morning, and oppress the poor out of the land,
verses.8:5: saying, "When will the month pass, that we may trade, and the Sabbaths, that we may open the storehouse, to make the measure small, and to make the weight great, and to make an unjust balance,
verses.8:6: to buy even the poor for silver, and the humble in exchange for sandals, and we will trade from every produce?"
verses.8:7: The Lord swears by the pride of Jacob: "Surely all your works shall never be forgotten!
verses.8:8: And shall not the land be troubled because of these things, and everyone who dwells in it mourn? And destruction shall rise up like a river, and shall go down like the river of Egypt."
verses.8:9: "And it shall come to pass in that day," says the Lord, the Lord, "that the sun shall go down at noon, and the light shall grow dark upon the earth in the daytime.
verses.8:10: And I will turn your feasts into mourning, and all your songs into lamentation; and I will bring sackcloth upon every waist, and baldness upon every head; and I will make him like the mourning for a beloved one, and those who are with him like a day of anguish."
verses.8:11: "Behold, the days are coming," says the Lord, "when I will send forth a famine upon the land—not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but a famine of hearing the word of the Lord.
verses.8:12: And the waters of the sea shall be shaken, and from the north even to the east they shall run about, seeking the word of the Lord, and they shall by no means find it.
verses.8:13: In that day the fair virgins and the young men shall faint in thirst,
verses.8:14: those who swear by the propitiation of Samaria, and those who say, 'As your god lives, O Dan!' and, 'As your god lives, O Beersheba!' And they shall fall, and shall by no means rise again."
verses.9:1: I saw the Lord standing upon the altar, and He said, "Strike upon the mercy seat, and the porches shall be shaken, and cut through upon the heads of all; and the remnant of them I will slay with the sword. No fugitive among them shall escape, and no survivor among them shall be delivered.
verses.9:2: Though they hide themselves in Hades, from there My hand shall draw them up; and though they ascend into heaven, from there I will bring them down;
verses.9:3: though they conceal themselves on the summit of Carmel, from there I will search them out and take them; and though they plunge down from My eyes into the depths of the sea, there I will command the dragon, and it shall bite them;
verses.9:4: and though they go into captivity before the face of their enemies, there I will command the sword, and it shall slay them; and I will set My eyes upon them for evil and not for good."
verses.9:5: And the Lord, the Lord God Almighty—He who touches the earth and shakes it, and all who dwell in it shall mourn, and its destruction shall rise up like a river, and shall go down like the river of Egypt;
verses.9:6: He who builds His ascent into heaven and founds His promise upon the earth, He who summons the water of the sea and pours it out upon the face of the earth—the Lord Almighty is His name.
verses.9:7: "Are you not like the sons of the Ethiopians to Me, O sons of Israel?" says the Lord. "Did I not bring up Israel from the land of Egypt, and the foreigners from Cappadocia, and the Syrians from the pit?
verses.9:8: Behold, the eyes of the Lord God are upon the kingdom of the sinners, and I will remove it from the face of the earth; yet I will not utterly remove the house of Jacob," says the Lord.
verses.9:9: "For I command, and I will winnow the house of Israel among all the nations, just as winnowing is done in a winnowing basket, and no broken fragment shall fall upon the earth.
verses.9:10: All the sinners of My people shall die by the sword, those who say, 'The evil things shall by no means draw near nor come upon us.'
verses.9:11: In that day I will raise up the fallen tabernacle of David, and I will rebuild its fallen parts, and its demolished places I will raise up, and I will rebuild it as in the days of old,
verses.9:12: so that the remnant of mankind may earnestly seek, and all the nations upon whom My name has been called," says the Lord who performs these things.
verses.9:13: "Behold, the days are coming," says the Lord, "when the grain harvest shall overtake the vintage, and the grape shall ripen at seedtime; and the mountains shall drip with sweet wine, and all the hills shall be thickly planted;
verses.9:14: and I will restore the captivity of My people Israel, and they shall build the wasted cities and dwell in them; and they shall plant a vineyard and drink their wine, and they shall plant gardens and eat their fruits;
verses.9:15: and I will plant them upon their own land, and they shall by no means ever again be uprooted from the land which I have given them," says the Lord God Almighty.

notes.1:1: The Greek text reads "in Accarim" (treating the Hebrew word for herdsmen as a place name) and "concerning Jerusalem" (where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "concerning Israel").
notes.1:3: The Greek renders the recurring refrain "I will not turn away from him/her/them" (agreeing with each nation) and reads "sawed with iron saws the women with child" rather than "threshed with iron sledges."
notes.1:5: The Greek reads "son of Hader" in verse 4 (for Ben-hadad), "a tribe from the men of Haran" (for "the scepter-holder from Beth-eden"), and "the called people of Syria" (reading Hebrew "to Kir" as "called").
notes.1:6: The Greek reads "the captivity of Solomon" (also in verse 9), reading the Hebrew word for "whole" or "complete" as the name Solomon.
notes.1:11: The Greek diverges markedly from the Hebrew here, reading "ravaged a mother upon the earth" (for "stifled his compassion") and "seized his shuddering for a testimony, and kept his onslaught for victory."
notes.2:3: The Greek text reads simply "all who belong to it" without an explicit noun for "rulers" or "princes."
notes.2:7: In Greek, "that tread upon the dust of the earth" is neuter plural modifying "sandals" from verse 6, followed by "struck the heads of the poor with fists" and "the name of their God."
notes.2:8: The Greek reads "binding their garments with cords, they made curtains," interpreting the Hebrew word for pledged garments as "cords."
notes.2:16: The Greek reads "shall not find his heart in mighty deeds," and uses the verb dioxetai (normally "pursue," here used intransitively in the sense of "flee" or "rush away").
notes.3:3: The Greek reads "unless they make themselves known to one another," reflecting a Hebrew reading "be known" rather than "agree" or "meet by appointment."
notes.3:7: The Greek reads paideian ("instruction" or "discipline") where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "His secret counsel."
notes.3:9: The Greek reads "regions among the Assyrians" (for Hebrew "citadels in Ashdod") and "many wondrous things" (for "great tumults").
notes.3:11: The Greek reads "Tyre" (Tyros), taking the Hebrew consonantal text for "adversary" (tsar) as the name of the city Tyre.
notes.3:12: The Greek reads "opposite the tribe, and in Damascus the priests," differing sharply from the Hebrew imagery of the corner of a couch and a bed.
notes.3:15: The Greek renders the winter house as "the colonnaded house" (peripteron) and concludes with "many other houses shall be added" (reading the Hebrew verb for "come to an end" as "be added").
notes.4:2: The Greek text reads plural "His holy things" (ton hagion autou), "with weapons" (en hoplois), and "fiery pestilent men" (empyroi loimoi), and in 4:3 names "Mount Romman" (to oros to Rhomman), diverging notably from the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.4:4: The Septuagint uses past-tense verbs ("You entered... and acted ungodly") rather than ironic imperatives, and in 4:5 renders "they read the law outside" (anegnosan exo nomon).
notes.4:10: The Greek reads "in fire" and "in your wrath" (en te orge hymon), reflecting the double sense of the underlying Hebrew word meaning both "nostril" and "wrath."
notes.4:13: The Septuagint famously reads "His Anointed" (ton christon autou, literally "His Christ") and "creates spirit" (ktizon pneuma, which can also mean "wind").
notes.5:3: The Greek doubles the divine title as kyrios Kyrios ("the Lord, the Lord"), rendering the Hebrew compound title.
notes.5:5: The Greek translates the place name Beersheba literally as "the Well of the Oath" (to phrear tou horkou).
notes.5:7: In the Greek text, verses 7 through 9 form a continuous doxology praising the Lord ("He who executes judgment on high... who makes all things and transforms them"), differing from the Masoretic Text.
notes.5:14: The Greek connects "just as you have said" at the close of verse 14 directly to the people's claim in verse 15 ("We have hated evil things and loved good things").
notes.5:26: The Septuagint names "Moloch" and "Rephan" (Raiphan), a form echoed in Stephen's quotation of this passage in Acts 7:43.
notes.6:2: The Greek reads "all of you" (pantes) rather than the city name Calneh, and "Gath of the foreigners" (allophylon), the standard Septuagint designation for the Philistines.
notes.6:3: The Septuagint reads "who come to an evil day" and "false sabbaths" (sabbaton pseudon), reflecting a different reading of the underlying Hebrew text.
notes.6:7: The Greek text has the distinctive reading "the neighing of horses shall be removed from Ephraim" (chremetismos hippon ex Ephraim).
notes.6:12: The Greek asks "Shall they keep silent among mares?" (ei parasiopesontai en theleiais), reflecting a different sense of the Hebrew root meaning both "plow" and "be silent."
notes.6:14: The Greek renders the southern boundary as "the torrent of the west" (tou cheimarrou ton dysmon), translating the Hebrew term for the Arabah by way of the related word for "evening" or "west."
notes.7:1: The Septuagint reads "one creeping locust—Gog the king," a major textual divergence from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's "after the king's mowings."
notes.7:3: The Greek uses the imperative "Relent" (literally "Repent") as a continuation of Amos's plea—and likewise in 7:6—whereas the Hebrew reports in narrative past tense that the Lord relented.
notes.7:7: Greek adamas ("adamant," an exceedingly hard stone or metal) stands here and in 7:8 where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has a term commonly translated "plumb line" or "tin."
notes.7:9: "Altars of laughter" preserves the Septuagint's literal translation of the Hebrew name Isaac as gelos ("laughter").
notes.7:17: In this Greek versification, the opening clause of the fourth vision ("Thus the Lord, the Lord showed me") concludes 7:17, so chapter 8 begins at 8:2.
notes.8:2: Greek angos ixeutou ("a fowler's basket") reflects a distinct Septuagint reading where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "a basket of summer fruit."
notes.8:3: Greek phatnomata ("paneled ceilings") stands where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "the songs of the temple."
notes.8:12: The Septuagint reads "the waters of the sea shall be shaken," whereas the Hebrew reads "they shall wander from sea to sea."
notes.8:14: "Propitiation of Samaria" renders Greek hilasmos (where the Hebrew has "guilt of Samaria"), and the Greek reads "your god, O Beersheba" where the Hebrew reads "the way of Beersheba."
notes.9:1: Greek hilasterion ("mercy seat" or "propitiatory") translates a Hebrew term usually rendered "capitals" of the temple pillars.
notes.9:6: Greek epangelian ("promise") stands where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "His vault."
notes.9:7: The Septuagint uses "the foreigners" (allophyloi, its standard term for the Philistines), "Cappadocia" (for Hebrew Caphtor), and "the pit" (bothros, for Hebrew Kir).
notes.9:12: The Septuagint reads "that the remnant of mankind may earnestly seek" (famous from its citation in Acts 15:17, whereas the Hebrew reads "that they may possess the remnant of Edom"); no direct object is stated after the verb in the Greek here.
notes.9:13: The Septuagint's harvest imagery—"the grain harvest shall overtake the vintage," "the grape shall ripen at seedtime," and "all the hills shall be thickly planted"—differs in wording from the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
